chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Suleyman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Mushaf (copies of the Quran) shall not be bought (for a price). So when you buy, say:
I am only buying from you the paper, and whatever is in it from the leather/cover, and its decoration, and whatever is in it from the work of your hands, for such and such (amount).'

key_terms.الْمَصَاحِفَ: The copies of the Quran (plural of Mushaf)

ai.seo_question: How to properly buy a Quran copy according to Shia hadith to avoid selling the Quran itself?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudential concept of *Istihlak* (subsumption), where the Quran is treated as an intrinsic attribute of the physical vessel rather than a separate commodity to be sold. By specifying the purchase of paper, leather, and craftsmanship, the Imam (peace be upon him) preserves the sanctity of the scripture while facilitating its commercial circulation, a nuance critical to distinguishing between the divine word and its material medium.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Parchment (Holy Quran) must never be bought (for a price). So whenever you (have to) buy, so say, ‘But rather I am buying from you the paper and whatever is therein from the cover and its decor and whatever is in it from the work of your hands (printing etc.), for such and such (an amount)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn Sulayman who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Pages (of al-Quran) can never be bought; if you buy say, ‘I buy from you the sheet and whatever is in it, like skin and decoration and the work of your hand for such and such amount.’”
